description: We are ambitious learners and we love to explore. We are interested in astronomy, coding and graphic designing.
summary:
**BEYOND THE VOID** is a 2.5D retro sci-fi survival game built in HTML5/Canvas and WebAudio where players take on the role of an astronaut stranded on the Moon after orbital debris destroys their Mars-bound spacecraft. Guided by **Astrokat**, an expressive AI companion, players must survive a 30-day countdown until NASA’s rescue lander arrives.

The game addresses the challenge by turning real aerospace engineering principles into intuitive, kid-friendly gameplay. Players balance finite generator fuel to sustain oxygen and suit power, schedule extravehicular scavenging during 2-minute daylight windows before retreating indoors for 1-minute nights, and repair six perimeter radar outposts to build a distributed telemetry and defense network. Through environmental storytelling—unlocking caves on Day 27 to uncover lost expedition logs—the game culminates in a plot twist where the terrifying night stalker, **The Hollow**, proves to be a guardian helping defeat **The Void**.

This project matters because it makes complex space-habitat logistics—such as closed-loop life support, power budgeting, and communication relays—accessible and memorable to young learners, proving that survival in space depends on strategic foresight, resilience, and looking past surface appearances.
details:
Here is a much more natural, grounded, and human-sounding version of the project details—written the way a passionate student/developer team would actually explain their hackathon game to judges, without stiff buzzwords.

What It Does & How It Works

BEYOND THE VOID is a 2.5D retro sci-fi survival game we built for the NASA Space Apps Hackathon. The story kicks off with a short animated cutscene: your crew is on a research trip to Mars when unexpected space debris destroys your ship, leaving you stranded on the Moon with 30 days to survive before NASA’s rescue team can reach you. Your only company is Astrokat, a cheerful little AI cat in a space suit who talks you through the basics and helps you stay alive.

The gameplay runs on a fast real-time loop—2 minutes of daylight followed by 1 minute of night:

  • During the day, you run out across a cratered lunar map to scavenge scrap metal, crystals, and fuel cells. You have to keep an eye out for The Void, a massive blue-white cosmic entity that shows up once or twice a day—if you spot it, your only rule is to sprint straight back to base.
  • At night, you stay inside your base dome to craft gear at the workbench or sleep in a crafted pod to skip to morning. If you step outside in the dark, a shadowy purple creature called The Hollow attacks and forces you back inside.
  • Keeping the lights on & exploring: You feed collected fuel into your base generator to keep your oxygen flowing and recharge your suit battery. Around the map, there are six broken radar outposts you can repair to push back the fog-of-war, spot threats earlier, and earn protective shields. Once you reach Day 27, the caves at the north and south ends of the map unlock—letting you find the crashed remains and diary logs of a previous lost crew. Those logs reveal the big twist: The Hollow wasn't trying to hurt you. It was keeping you locked inside at night to protect you from The Void. On Day 30, when The Void tries to block the NASA rescue ship from landing, The Hollow teams up with you for the final boss fight.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Learning real space survival by playing: Instead of reading a textbook about how astronauts survive off-world, players feel it firsthand. If you forget to refuel the generator, your oxygen drops. If you stay out too late scavenging, you get caught in the dark. Fixing the six radar stations shows how relay networks keep deep-space explorers safe.
  • Approachable for younger players: Space survival games can feel intimidating or overly dark, so we paired the eerie cosmic mystery with soft, kid-friendly UI—a 7-heart health bar, rounded dialogue boxes, and Astrokat cracking jokes and giving gentle reminders.
  • Playable anywhere in seconds: Because the entire game lives inside a single browser file, anyone—judges, teachers, or kids—can open it and start playing immediately without downloading or installing anything.

Tools, Languages & Software We Used

  • HTML5, CSS3 & Vanilla JavaScript: We wrote the entire game from scratch in plain JavaScript so it stays lightweight, fast, and easy to run in any web browser.
  • HTML5 2D Canvas: Used to build a tilted 3D isometric lunar island, glowing radar beams, particle trails, and our custom chibi pixel-art characters and item icons.
  • Web Audio API: Instead of loading heavy MP3 files, we programmed retro synth sound effects directly in code—laser blasts, mining clinks, thruster hums, and warning alarms.
  • AI Art Ideation: We used AI image generation early on to brainstorm our color palette (deep purples, blacks, and electric blues) and nail down the cute-meets-creepy chibi look for Astrokat, The Hollow, and The Void.
  • Hardware: Built and tested on standard laptops using simple keyboard (WASD/Arrows, E, Space) and mouse controls.

What Makes It Creative

  • Flipping the "monster in the dark" cliché: Almost every survival game trains you that daylight is safe and monsters come out at night. We wanted to mess with that instinct. Players spend 29 days terrified of The Hollow, only to realize right before the finale that it was actually guarding them the whole time.
  • Cute UI meets creepy space mystery: Watching a giant, horned shadow entity emerge from a crater while an adorable pixel cat in star-shaped headphones cheers you on creates a fun contrast that keeps the game tense without ever becoming too scary for kids.

What Our Team Considered While Building It

  • Making a 30-day game playable in a 3-minute hackathon pitch: Nobody has an hour to play 30 full days during a live demo, so we kept the day/night cycles brisk (3 minutes total per day) and built quick-jump demo buttons right into the HUD so judges can test nighttime, the Day 27 cave logs, or the Day 30 boss fight whenever they want.
  • Clear visual feedback: When you're managing oxygen, suit battery, generator fuel, and monster sightings all at once, it's easy to get confused. We spent extra time making sure the bars, icons, and Astrokat's speech bubble clearly tell you why you're taking damage and what you need to fix next.
  • Balancing realism with fun: We grounded the mechanics in real NASA concepts—life-support power budgets, EVA time limits, and radar relays—while still letting players craft plasma cannons and energy lightsabers so the final boss fight feels genuinely exciting.
